sections.title: Describing produce
sections.content: At the market you choose with your eyes. Colours and ripeness are adjectives, like *friss* and *édes*. Used alone as a description they come after the noun, and Hungarian needs no word for "is": *A paradicsom piros.* Join two descriptions with *és*, set them against each other with *de*, and add *nagyon* for "very": *A citrom nagyon savanyú, de a banán édes.*

items.english: The banana is yellow and ripe.
The pear is green, but sweet.

items.spanish: A citrom sárga és nagyon savanyú.
items.english: The lemon is yellow and very sour.
The apple is red and fresh.

sections.content: *Érett* is for fruit and vegetables that ripen. Bread, fish or milk are *friss* (fresh) instead. Before a noun these words never change: *piros*, *zöld*, *sárga*.
